thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: cont-batch path p99 latency spike detected in us-west-2 (metrics window 22:07 UTC). p99 = 11.2s, p95 = 1.8s, streaming stalls increased, HTTP 503 up ~12% in last 5m. Affected tenants: tenant-alpha, tenant-omega, tenant-gamma. Creating thread for triage and live mitigation.

ashlee: ack. I'm oncall. paging tyler and mira to triage. I'll grab customer impact and coord comms.

tyler: on it. pulling tail logs. seeing big pack formation and queuing on cont-batch scheduler. pack wait times shot up.

mira: I see the same on runtime dashboards — long-running batches with highly heterogeneous seq lengths (some >6k tokens) are dominating GPU time. KV cache churn + paging observed. suspect mixed-seqlen amplification.

ignacio: any recent model/kernel rollouts or scheduler changes in the last hour?

ashlee: no model rollouts. infra autoscaler did a gentle downscale ~30m ago in us-west-2 due to memory pressure. not sure if related.

cale: CS: three customers reported streaming freezes, one reported 30% error rate on streaming endpoints. customer-alpha is asking for immediate status. escalating to priority.

ops-bot: mitigation checklist suggestion:
- temporarily reduce cont-batch batch_max_size and batch_max_tokens
- enable sequence-fair scheduling to avoid large-seq monopolizing packs
- route streaming requests with seq_len > 2048 to a small-window serving variant
- consider short-lived dedicated pool for the worst-affected tenant

tyler: I'll apply a quick config change to reduce pack sizes and prioritize streaming.

tyler: applying change now.
```bash
# reduce batch size and enable seq-fair scheduling
redwoodctl set-config --pool cont-batch --batch_max_size 32 --batch_max_tokens 64 --enable_seqfair true
# route heavy streaming to small-window model
redwoodctl route update --match 'streaming && seq_len>2048' --target 'lm-small-window-v1'
```

ashlee: running the commands. will monitor.

mira: runtime metrics — KV eviction rate drops after config apply, swap usage reduced. p99 trending down.

tyler: quick check: p99 dropped from 11.2s -> 2.1s within two minutes of the change. p95 is stable ~1.5s. streaming stalls decreased but tenant-omega still shows intermittent 5-8s spikes.

ashlee: tenant-omega looks like the largest contributor to mixed-seq tail. Can we carve them into a temp dedicated pool while we investigate workload shape?

ignacio: provisioning a short-lived dedicated pool for tenant-omega now: `redwoodctl create-pool --name tmp-ded-omega --gpu a100-s --replicas 2` ETA ~3m. will also add a routing rule to send their traffic to the pool.

cale: notifying affected customers with current status and ETA for mitigation. using the "live-incident" template.

ops-bot: alternate fallback: if latency persists after pool, consider routing to quantized variant or limiting per-tenant concurrency: `--max_concurrency 8` for the tenant.

mira: digging into root cause hypothesis: mixed sequence lengths from tenant-omega + downscale reduced available parallelism -> larger batches form, KV cache gets cold/evicts -> paging and stalls. Scheduler fairness amplification then amplifies tail.

tyler: agreed. next steps proposed:
1) keep reduced batch_max_size and seq-fair scheduling for 1 hour.
2) keep temporary dedicated pool for tenant-omega until load normalizes.
3) run perf regression tests against mixed-seq synthetic traffic.
4) update autoscaler policy to avoid aggressive downscale during known high-mix traffic windows.
5) postmortem owner: ashlee.

ashlee: handoff to night oncall leah at 00:00 UTC. leah pls monitor p99 and the dedicated pool. set me as contact if we need escalation. :thumbsup:

leah: ack. I'll monitor dashboards and keep alerts active (p99>3s page). will decommission tmp-ded-omega after 30m of stable p99<2s.

tyler: logging current mitigation commands and outputs to the incident runbook. saving relevant traces and flamegraphs for the postmortem.

ashlee: customer comms in flight. CS queued follow-ups. once stable we'll do a targeted follow-up with tenant-omega to review request patterns (bursting, very long prompts).

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigated (live mitigation applied). tracking to postmortem.

ashlee: thanks all. meeting for a quick 15m sync in #eng-runtime in 30m to cover durable fixes (scheduler tuning, autoscaler changes, tenant isolation patterns).

(End of thread)
